description: Observations from hand-written probe programs run with the pinned QCP binary symexec (`--full-auto --no-exec-info --basic-assertion`), env cleared, in a scratch directory. Probes are small and not exhaustive; they establish why the common projection is restricted, not general QCP limits.
binary: symexec from sensuschung/malice commit 4675d37c (sha256 in malice_provenance.json)

probes.program: long x=0; for i<n: x+=2; Inv x==2*i && 0<=i<=n@pre; Ensure __return == 2*n

probes.result: 'Safety Check Failed' at the overflowing statement: QCP checks signed int overflow
type error 'Cannot unify types Assertion and Z'; used `Ensure __return == __return` instead

probes.program: unsigned char a+=84 with Inv 0<=a<=255 (also unsigned short, unsigned, xor on unsigned char, unsigned *=3)
probes.result: exit 139 (segfault) even though the programs are well defined
'Safety Check Failed' (modulo not handled in the safety check)

probes.program: nested for with inner Inv `0<=x && x<=12000*i + 4*j ...` (several equivalent spellings)
probes.result: exit 139 (segfault); inner Inv without the product term fails normally; equality form with 4*m@pre*i fails safety

consequence: Common projection limited to int/long programs with + - * comparisons and if/else whose ground-truth invariant QCP verifies; of 21 candidate safe programs only 8 qualified (ground-truth validation in malice_ground_truth_validation.json).
